read-the-registry-page-generated-from-th.text: Read the registry page generated from the chain.

As Alice, you hold a registry's state token and the packaged release, and nothing else: no wallet file of yours, nothing from the person who created the registry. You run one command and read which registry this is, which release it runs, what its rules are and what it holds now. As Bob, on your own machine, you run the same command: reading the same chain state with the same release gives you the same bytes. As an integrator, you want to know what the page does not prove, and the page says so itself.

A program reads the same facts with the json switch:

The command takes the state token, the blueprint of the packaged release, a provider and a network. It takes no wallet, no signing key, no state directory and no file of any actor; any other setting is refused by name before anything is read. The version label comes from the version file beside the blueprint. From an extracted release archive, run the archive's own singular with its blueprint and the adjacent version file: the Demo 1 journey reads the page this way right after create, from the command the create receipt printed. A success prints the page alone and writes no file; every refusal prints one JSON receipt and exits non-zero.
The page carries no clock, no chain tip and no session identity, so identical inputs give identical bytes. Pending requests appear in one fixed order. The text and the JSON carry the same fields.

what-the-page-does-not-prove.text: What the page does not prove.

The provenance line says it in fixed text: the page shows the public history of the state token from create to the live state output, each fold's rebuilt root checked against the root recorded in that fold's state datum, and nothing beyond it. The history was read from Koios. The provider's answers are unverified: raw facts and untrusted reconstruction material, no ledger proofs and no anchor. The release label is the archive's own claim. The page is unsigned.

refusals.text: A refusal prints one JSON receipt on standard output with a non-zero exit status, as every command does.

what-is-not-in-this-page.text: What is not in this page.

A block anchor for the last fold waits on its own provider read. The documentation links are computed from the claimed version, not checked against a published asset. The independently derived action identity in the public report waits on its own slice. None of these changes what the page shows; each arrives separately.
